chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Marwan ibn Ubayd, from Jamil ibn Amr, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me:

"What is 'Allah is Greater'?" I said: "Allah is Greater than everything." He said: "Was there a thing such that He is Greater than it?" I said: "Then what is it?" He said: "Allah is Greater than to be described."
ai.seo_question: What is the deeper theological meaning of 'Allah is Greater' beyond being greater than creation?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refines the understanding of 'Allahu Akbar' by moving beyond comparative magnitude to divine ineffability. He illustrates that while God is greater than any conceivable entity, His essence transcends all human description and conceptual limitation, a key concept in Shia theology known as *ta'til al-sifat* (negation of anthropomorphic attributes). This highlights the balance between affirming God's greatness and recognizing His absolute transcendence (*tanzih*).

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Yahya al-‘Attar, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin ‘Isa, from his father, from Maruk bin ‘Ubayd, from Jumay’ bin Amru, that he said: Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said to me:

What thing is: «Allah is Greater»?» [1] I said: Allah is Greater than everything. Then he said: Was there a particular thing to which He is Greater? Then I said: Then what is it? He said: Allah is Greater than to be described.
